text: Forgot how important it is to take a step back when you feel yourself overtrading. Back in the beginning of June I was at a low point in terms of my discipline and approach to trading as a whole. Many leaks in the boat and simply didn't have the hunger for multiple months to accumulate the screen time needed to perform with the best. Over the past month, did I reach the screen time required to have my pulse on the market? Yes Was it fully utilized to the best of my abilities and stuck to my foundational processes? No The ying yang effect of mastering hunger and discipline will forever be the success combination that separates the greats from elites over a long enough time horizon. To play onchain at the highest level you need to have the fire in your belly to wake up and do 14 hours, day after day with zero or sometimes negative results. In my case I usually need 6-8 weeks of this to truly peak in potential. On the contrary, having the emotional control to stick to your processes no matter how good of a read you have and/or believe in an obvious thesis. It's only been 29 days since Ansem started. If you've participated to the best of your abilities, I'm sure this past month has felt like six. While our brain plays tricks on us due to seeing 8/9 fig runners on a daily basis, the rotations have been more brutal than any other time in past memory. Guilt overcomes your consciousness when you attempt to take a step back, someone in your gc is up mid 6 figs in 24 hours, the timeline is filled with KOL's who hit the obvious trade that you were somehow stupid enough not to take with hindsight bias. There comes a point where your edge erodes as these small voices grow louder and push you into desperation to catch the next runner. You lose flow state and every move you make feels aggressive and mechanical, there's no synchrony between your spirit and faith. How do you recognize this? Not easily. A mix of journalling, documenting trades/PnL and the gut feeling that you're doing the right things but heading in the wrong direction. One of my favourite quotes is from Rafa Nadal when he said by pushing his body to the absolute limit and making risky health decisions on the edge of right and wrong, he earned his record breaking legacy. Without taking those extreme paths to manage his chronic foot pain, he might have had 10 or 12 fewer Grand Slams. While Tennis and trading shitcoins couldn't seem further apart, I do think there's many correlations in the mental gymnastics we perform on a daily basis. Isolated environment for hours on end, the tinniest error in precision can cost you the match, you can play your absolute best then still fall apart if you don't execute the final step, the winner is the person who keeps the ball going back net with unforced errors/survives till the next trade or meta. There's no worse feeling than losing your pulse on the market, except being so convinced you're one trade away from a home run that you burn yourself into the ground.
